title: Review into Public Disclosure of Full NRIC Numbers on Bizfile People Search
what_it_is: Review into Public Disclosure of Full NRIC Numbers on Bizfile People Search

sections.label: Bizfile full NRIC numbers paywall
sections.summary: The new Bizfile portal displayed full NRIC numbers in People Search, causing public anxiety, so People Search was disabled on 13 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The People Profile function sits behind a paywall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But unlike the old Bizfile portal, which showed partial National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) numbers in the People Search results, the new Bizfile portal displayed full NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: This caused public anxiety about how easily full NRIC numbers could be searched for and accessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Therefore, the People Search function was disabled on the night of 13 December 2024.

sections.label: Panel report accepted by Minister
sections.summary: The Panel submitted its report on 25 February 2025, and the Minister accepted its findings and recommendations and reported this to the Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Panel submitted its report to me on 25 February 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I reviewed the report and reported to the Prime Minister that I had accepted its findings and recommendations.

sections.label: Report made public
sections.summary: The report was made public on 3 March 2025, giving Members the opportunity to study it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Hon Members would have had the opportunity to study the report, which was made public on 3 March 2025.

sections.label: MDDI circular on NRIC use
sections.summary: On 5 July 2024, MDDI issued a Circular Minute to public agencies to stop using NRIC numbers for authentication and move away from partial NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On 5 July 2024, MDDI issued a Circular Minute (CM) to public agencies to stop the use of NRIC numbers for authentication and to start moving away from the use of partial NRIC numbers.

sections.label: ACRA misunderstood MDDI instruction
sections.summary: ACRA misunderstood MDDI's July 2024 instruction to cease planned use of masked NRIC numbers, interpreting it as requiring full disclosure in People Search.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: ACRA misunderstood MDDI's instruction in the July 2024 CM for agencies to "immediately cease any planned use of masked NRIC numbers, for example, in new business processes or digital products".

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: ACRA interpreted this as a requirement to "unmask" or disclose NRIC numbers in full in the People Search function on the new Bizfile portal.

sections.label: ACRA instructed IT vendor
sections.summary: Based on its interpretation, ACRA instructed its IT vendor on 17 August 2024 to display NRIC numbers in full in People Search, launched 9 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Based on ACRA's interpretation of the July 2024 CM, ACRA then instructed its IT vendor on 17 August 2024 to make the requisite system changes to display NRIC numbers in full in the People Search function on the new Bizfile portal, which was then launched on 9 December 2024.

sections.label: ACRA NRIC disclosure breach
sections.summary: ACRA disclosed full NRIC numbers in People Search without assessing the balance, contravening IM8 rules it had to comply with under the PSGA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Fourth, in deciding to disclose full NRIC numbers in People Search, ACRA did not first assess the proper balance between sharing full NRIC numbers and ensuring that they were not too readily accessible on the People Search function.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: This contravened the Government's internal rules on data management, namely, IM8, which ACRA was required to comply with under the Public Sector (Governance) Act (or PSGA).

sections.label: People Search security features
sections.summary: The Panel found People Search made NRIC numbers too easily available, and some security features were not adequately implemented at the 9 December 2024 launch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Panel found that the design of the People Search function of the new Bizfile portal made individuals' NRIC numbers too easily available to those who were improperly using the People Search function in a way that went beyond its intended purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: ACRA had required its IT vendor to implement various security features in the People Search function of the new Bizfile portal to protect against unintended uses by, for instance, limiting the extent of searches allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: However, certain security features were not adequately implemented when the new Bizfile portal was launched on 9 December 2024.

sections.label: CAPTCHA and script retrieval
sections.summary: Some security features including CAPTCHA were not adequately implemented, allowing script-based data retrieval from 9 to 13 December 2024, rectified before service resumed on 28 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The review found that some security features, including the CAPTCHA functionality, were not adequately implemented, allowing potential data retrieval using scripts from 9 to 13 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: These security issues were rectified by the vendor in the revised People Search function before it resumed service on 28 December 2024.

sections.label: Slower incident fact-finding
sections.summary: After public feedback, ACRA and MDDI should have ascertained the key facts more quickly and ACRA should have disabled People Search sooner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Upon receiving the public feedback, ACRA and MDDI should have ascertained more quickly the key facts of how the Bizfile incident happened and ACRA should have disabled the People Search function sooner.

sections.label: Ministers accept responsibility
sections.summary: Ministers Josephine Teo and Indranee Rajah have publicly accepted overall responsibility and apologised for what happened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Both Ministers Josephine Teo and Indranee Rajah have publicly accepted this overall responsibility and also apologised for what has happened.

sections.label: Measures against officers
sections.summary: Agencies found no malicious or wilful wrongdoing but inadequacies in judgement and actions, and are taking measures from counselling to retraining to performance grade reductions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The agencies have assessed that while there was no malicious or wilful wrongdoing by the officers, there were inadequacies in their judgement and actions, and appropriate measures are being taken against them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: These measures range from counselling to retraining to reductions in performance grade, which will carry financial consequences, such as a reduction in their performance-based payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: As for ACRA's contravention of IM8, PSGA does not prescribe financial penalties for public agencies that contravene IM8, and there is a good reason for that.

sections.label: Ministerial responsibility for ACRA and MDDI
sections.summary: The Ministers overseeing ACRA and Smart Nation work in MDDI had overall responsibility, and the Prime Minister will consider the incident in evaluating the Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Ministers overseeing ACRA as well as the Smart Nation work in MDDI had overall responsibility for the organisations under their charge and the Prime Minister will take into account this incident in his evaluation of the Ministers.

sections.label: ACRA communication list unclear
sections.summary: It is not clear from the report whether ACRA provided a list of all existing communication and correspondence with the public using masked NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: [Please refer to "Explanation and Impact of Policy Change on Full NRIC Number and Further Measures on Public Education and Protection of Sensitive Identifiable Information", Official Report, 7 January 2025, Vol 95, Issue 148, Oral Answers to Questions section.] The first pertains to the CM of 5 July and this is found at pages 20 and 21 of the report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is not clear from the report whether ACRA provided a list of all existing communication and correspondence with members of the public that used masked NRIC numbers.

sections.label: ACRA sought clarification from MDDI
sections.summary: The report states ACRA sought clarification from MDDI on how the July CM applied to its new Bizfile portal, and an officer asked about removing NRIC masking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At page 15 of the report, it states that from 5 July – that was the point in time when the CM was distributed – to early August, ACRA had, "sought clarification from MDDI on how the July CM should apply to ACRA's new Bizfile portal," which was the one launched on 9 December.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the report, I note at paragraph 48, it states that on 30 July, an ACRA officer, who had not gone for the MDDI briefing and did not see the FAQ document that MDDI had emailed; and this officer asked MDDI if ACRA needed to cater system enhancements to remove the masking of NRIC numbers in the People Search function.

sections.label: Independent assessment of NRIC unmasking
sections.summary: The report's conclusion states ACRA did not first assess the proper balance between sharing full NRIC numbers and ensuring they were not too readily accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Was there any independent assessment done about the full unmasking of NRIC numbers on the People Search function?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I ask this question because in the conclusion of the report, it states that ACRA did not first assess the proper balance between sharing full NRIC numbers and ensuring that they were not too readily accessible.

sections.label: Gap in understanding between agencies
sections.summary: A gap in understanding between the two agencies was identified as one of the shortcomings in the report and the Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In fact, that is really what was identified as one of the shortcomings in the report and in my Statement just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There was a gap in understanding between the two agencies.

sections.label: PDPA and PSGA data rules
sections.summary: In the private sector there is the Personal Data Protection Act 2012, and in the public sector there is the PSGA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In the private sector, there is the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (or PDPA) and in the public sector there is the PSGA.

sections.label: Public sector data sharing expectation
sections.summary: In the public sector, there is an expectation of some sharing between the two to serve citizens better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In the public sector, there is an expectation that to serve citizens better, there is some sharing between the two.

sections.label: Financial penalties in PDPA and PSGA
sections.summary: PDPA financial penalties target the organisation, while penalties against a Government agency are not meaningful as funds come from the public purse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, that is an expectation and it is different between the private sector and the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There is another important difference, which is what the financial penalties are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: First of all, in the PDPA, the financial penalties are directed against the organisation; whereas in the PSGA, as I explained, if you direct the financial penalties against a Government agency, it is actually not very meaningful, because they all come, eventually, from the public purse.

sections.label: PDPA imported PSGA provisions
sections.summary: In 2020, the PDPA imported some PSGA provisions, allowing action against individuals in some circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Eventually, in 2020, the PDPA took some of the provisions in the PSGA and imported them into the PDPA, so that in some circumstances, the PDPA can be used to take action against individuals.

sections.label: ACRA resumes function without NRIC numbers
sections.summary: ACRA resumed service on that function without full or partial NRIC numbers after assessing intended users could be served without them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: ACRA has resumed service on that function, but without NRIC numbers, whether full or partial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Because they have done an assessment now and have come to the conclusion that it is possible to serve the intended users without having to use full or partial NRIC numbers, and that is what they have done.

sections.label: Shortcoming in internal communication
sections.summary: The Panel identified a shortcoming where MDDI's briefing position was not fully communicated internally, so ACRA and senior management decided without that information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: MDDI conducted a briefing, engaged the agencies, answered the questions and disseminated them the next day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There was a shortcoming that was identified by the Panel where they did not fully communicate internally what the position was.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And therefore, when ACRA and the senior management were making decisions on this, they were doing so without the benefit of the additional information that had come out of MDDI's briefings and interactions with the agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I think that describes how they had a difference of understanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But as Mr Liang indicated, there is a more important aspect here, which is that officers, especially at the senior level, need to understand the intent behind what the policy is – and certainly, officers at the senior level should be able to do so – and not implement things which are just going by the letter.

sections.label: Agencies and Prime Minister responsibility
sections.summary: Agencies remain responsible for what they do, and the Prime Minister is responsible for everything.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The agencies still have to be responsible for what they are doing, whatever season of the year it is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On the point of the Prime Minister's responsibility, well, the Prime Minister is responsible for everything.

sections.label: Lesson dissemination and crisis coordination
sections.summary: The report said lessons will be shared across the Public Service, and asked who would coordinate responses to similar or crisis incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In this case, it was shared in the report that the lessons will be disseminated to the broader Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Also, looking ahead, should there be similar incidents or other crisis-type of incidents happening, who will be coordinating the response and making sure that investigations and responses are being done in a timely manner?

sections.label: Enterprises using NRIC authentication
sections.summary: It asks about the progress of Government efforts to get enterprises still using NRIC numbers for authentication to rectify this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Given that there are still enterprises using the NRIC number as authentication, what is the progress of the Government's effort in getting them to rectify this?

sections.label: Public Service stopped NRIC authentication
sections.summary: The Public Service has stopped using NRIC for authentication, and guidance is going to private sector organisations to cease this unsafe practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On the enterprises' use of NRIC as authentication, the Public Service has stopped this practice within the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There is appropriate guidance going out to private sector organisations to also cease this practice because it is quite unsafe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: If there are private sector organisations which do not realise that they should stop using NRICs for authentication, I think they probably have not been paying any attention to the media on this issue at all.

sections.label: Sensitising agencies to database threats
sections.summary: It asks whether any searchable database attracts cyber troublemakers and how to sensitise agencies to dangers, especially databases with unchangeable NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, does the Senior Minister agree that in the modern era, we must assume that any database with a search function will attract cyber troublemakers trying to download and scrap as much of the information as possible?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And as such, how can we further strengthen the instincts or even the sixth sense within agencies and officers to be more sensitised to these dangers, especially for databases that contain NRICs, because the NRIC number is unique and cannot be changed?

sections.label: Portal vendor and security reviewer
sections.summary: It asks whether the same portal vendor and security reviewer serve other Government portals or organisations, and notes security must be considered in IT systems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this vein, do we know if the same portal vendor and the same security reviewer are providing services to any other Government portals or Government organisations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Specifically on IT security, yes, indeed, it is important that when organisations implement an IT system or change an IT system, that they take security into account.

sections.label: Vigilance, red teaming, bug bounty
sections.summary: It states the need for continued vigilance, and mentions a rigorous red teaming system and an evergreen bug bounty system inviting public help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, we need to keep on being vigilant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I should say, without going into too many details, because we do not want to give away exactly what we do in maintaining IT security, we do have a system of red teaming, which is quite rigorous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And we also invite the public to help us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We actually have a bug bounty system, one which is evergreen.

sections.label: Vendor selection and past performance
sections.summary: Vendors found not to have fulfilled responsibilities properly are taken into account in future tender awards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, indeed, we have a system for that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But for our process for choosing vendors, both IT vendors, as well as security vendors, I should say that if a vendor has been found to not have fulfilled his responsibilities properly, we take that into account in future awarding of tenders, because then, how can you be sure, as Dr Tan has pointed out.

sections.label: Vendor appointed independent security reviewer
sections.summary: Paragraphs 76 and 77 state the vendor, not ACRA, appointed the independent security reviewer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Paragraphs 76 and 77 of the report tells us that the vendor was the one who appointed the independent security reviewer, not ACRA.

sections.label: Moving away from NRIC numbers
sections.summary: The problems of using full and partial NRIC numbers are explained, so NRIC numbers should not be used as authenticators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And indeed, the issues and the problems of using full NRIC and partial NRIC numbers are explained there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: That is why we want to shift and make sure that we do not use NRIC numbers as authenticators and with regard to partial NRIC numbers, we should move away from that.

sections.label: Balancing ACRA registry and personal data
sections.summary: ACRA must balance its registry function promoting corporate transparency against protecting personal data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On the balance in ACRA, I would not say it is a conflict, but you have to strike the right balance between the functions that ACRA is meant to provide, which is to have a registry which promotes corporate transparency, and you have to balance that against how you protect personal data.

sections.label: Unresolved difference in interpretation
sections.summary: Both parties thought they understood, but an unresolved difference in interpretation resulted in the incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The fundamental issue was they both went away thinking that they understood what that was all about, but they had a difference in interpretation that was not resolved, resulting in this incident.

sections.label: Two terms understood differently
sections.summary: Two specific uses of terms were not understood in the same way by the two parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In this case, there were two specific uses of terms which the two did not understand in the same way.

sections.label: Partial NRIC numbers unmasking disagreement
sections.summary: MDDI said full NRIC numbers need not be unmasked in every case, while ACRA's leadership thought that was the direction to go.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And if I stop using partial NRIC numbers, what should I do with them?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And MDDI said, the intent was, you do not have to unmask the full NRIC number in every case; whereas ACRA's leadership thought that that was the direction to go.

sections.label: Bizfile People Search query surge
sections.summary: Over 500,000 queries were made on Bizfile's People Search between 9 and 13 December 2024, far exceeding the usual daily traffic of 2,000 to 3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, over 500,000 queries were made on the Bizfile portals' People Search between 9 and 13 December 2024, and this is far exceeding the usual daily traffic of 2,000 to 3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Has MDDI been monitoring, including on the dark web, for the sale of NRIC numbers, potentially exfiltrated during this period?

sections.label: Dark web NRIC monitoring
sections.summary: The dark web is monitored for a variety of things, including this, and no sale of NRIC numbers as such has been seen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In fact, we monitor the dark web for a variety of things, including this, and we have not seen any sale of NRIC numbers as such.

sections.label: Inter-Ministry Policy Coordination weakness
sections.summary: The question asks whether Senior Minister Teo finds the Inter-Ministry Policy Coordination and Implementation in this case weak.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My first question is, does Senior Minister Teo find that the Inter-Ministry Policy Coordination and Implementation in this case weak?

sections.label: Senior-level coordination for digital issues
sections.summary: The clarification asks whether coordination for PDPA, PSGA, cybersecurity and cybercrimes should be taken at Deputy Prime Minister or Senior Minister level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: My clarification is that, for important issues, like climate change and also earlier, the ageing population, we have Senior Minister-level and Deputy Prime Minister-level coordination, whether this whole class of issues on PDPA, PSGA, cybersecurity, cybercrimes should coordination be taken at a more senior level, at Deputy Prime Minister or Senior Minister level?

sections.label: Inter-Ministerial committee for scams
sections.summary: At that level, a system is set up for relevant agencies to work together, as with scams, where an inter-Ministerial committee was helmed by MHA political office holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: At that level, what we try and do is to make sure that we set up a system in which the relevant agencies work with each other properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, you will see that for scams, we were not very well-coordinated initially, but we did have an inter-Ministerial committee helmed by the Ministry of Home Affairs' political office holders, which brought all the different agencies together, including the banks and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), and engaged the platform companies.

sections.label: NRIC numbers as authenticators
sections.summary: The Member asked about identifier versus authenticator, and people used NRIC numbers as authenticators thinking they are secure and secret.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Member had a question on identifier versus authenticator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In fact, that is one of the misunderstandings that we have, which has led to this issue, because people began to use their NRIC numbers as authenticators, thinking that it is secure and secret.

sections.label: NRIC number purpose
sections.summary: The NRIC number is meant to refer to a person definitively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The NRIC number is meant to refer to you definitively.

sections.label: July 2024 CM email
sections.summary: Paragraph 40 of the report stated the July 2024 CM was emailed to senior Public Service Leaders, including those in IT and data matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: In paragraph 40 of the report, it was stated that this July 2024 CM was also emailed to senior Public Service Leaders, including those with key responsibilities in IT and data matters within their agencies.

sections.label: NRIC number not compromised
sections.summary: Nothing was seen on the dark web, and somebody knowing your NRIC number does not mean it is compromised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: No, we do not and have not seen anything, say, on the dark web, and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Which is that the fact that somebody knows your NRIC number, does not mean that it is compromised.

sections.label: Mistaken belief on NRIC security
sections.summary: Those not digitally-savvy mistakenly think NRIC numbers can be authenticators and partial NRIC numbers provide security, so this must be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Which leads me to partially answer Mr Leong's question, which is that it is precisely because those who are not so digitally-savvy have this mistaken impression that they can use the NRIC number as an authenticator, that partial NRIC numbers provide security, that we have to do this, because if we do not, then they will go away with this mistaken belief and continue to do so.

sections.label: Private sector authentication best practices
sections.summary: The Government wants the private sector to adopt best practices in authentication, and using NRIC as a password is unsafe and should be discouraged.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Of course, we should be adopting best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I think the Government does want the private sector to adopt best practices in authentication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And I am glad that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim agrees with that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And the idea that you can use your NRIC as your password is unsafe, and we want to discourage that and we hope that the private sector will stop that; we will see how we can reinforce that in a much clearer way for the private sector.

sections.label: Government review and lessons learned
sections.summary: The Government reviewed what happened, released a public report, and is sharing lessons across the Public Service to prevent recurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Government has conducted a thorough review over two months on what had happened, why they happened and how we can improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: A report has been released publicly and has been thoroughly discussed today in this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The lessons learned that the Panel has identified are also being disseminated across the whole of the Public Service, so that agencies can take these on board and ensure that similar incidents do not recur.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: This is so that the Government can account to the public and demonstrate its commitment to rectify shortcomings and serve the people better.

sections.label: Revised guillotine time
sections.summary: With the change in commencement time, the revised guillotine time for Head V, Ministry of Trade and Industry, is 2.25 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: With the change in commencement time, the revised guillotine time for Head V, Ministry of Trade and Industry, is 2.25 pm.
